annotations.title: In thy grandmother.
annotations.text: ◦ Though God ſhevv mercie to many that be of incredulous, heretical or ill parents, yet it is a goodly benediction of God to haue good education and to haue good faithful progenitors and Catholic parents. And it is a great ſinne to forſake the faith of our fathers that be Catholics, or contrarie to our education in the Church to folovv ſtrange doctrines, abandoning not only our next natural parents faith, but the ancient faith and belief of all our progenitors for many hundred years together. And if to folovv the faith of mother and grandmother only, the Chriſtian religion being then but nevvly planted, vvas ſo commendable euen in a Biſhop, how much more is it now laudable to cleaue faſt to the faith of ſo many our progenitors and ages that continued in the ſame Chriſtian religion vvhich they firſt receiued? [1] Our Proteſtants in their great wiſdom laugh at good ſimple men vvhen they talke of their fathers faith. But S. Hierom [2], I am a Chriſtian, ſaith he, and born of Chriſtian parents, and carie the ſign of the croſs in my forehead. And againe ep. 65. c. 3. Until this day the Chriſtian world hath been without this doctrine, that faith vvil I hold faſt being an old man, wherein I vvas born a child. And the holy Scriptures ſet vs often to ſchole to our fathers. [3] Aſke thy fathers, and they vvil ſhew thee, thy anceſtors, and they vvil tel thee. And againe, [4] Our fathers haue ſhevved vnto vs. And commonly the true God is called the God of the faithful and of their forefathers. Dan. 2. 3. And falſe gods and nevv doctrines or opinions be named, New and freſh, ſuch as their fathers worſhipped not. Deut. 32. Finally S. Paul both here and [5] often els allegeth for his defence and commendation, that he vvas of faithful progenitors. And it is a caſe that Heretics cannot lightly bragge of, no one ſect commonly during ſo long vvithout intermiſſion, that they can haue many progenitors of the ſaid ſect. Vvhich is a demonſtration that their faith is not true, and that it is impoſſible our Catholic faith to be falſe, ſuppoſing the Chriſtian religion to be true.

notes.text: The peoples speaches of their fathers faith, is very Christian and laudable.
A great blessing, to haue Catholike progenitors: and very commendable to cleaue fast to their faith.

annotations.title: Depoſitum.
annotations.text: ◦ A great comfort to al Chriſtians, that euery of their good deedes and ſufferings for Chriſt, and al the vvorldly loſſes ſuſteined for defenſe or confeſsion of their faith, be extant vvith God, and kept as depoſitum, to be repaied or receiued againe in heauen. Vvhich if the vvorldlings beleeued or conſidered, they vvould not ſo much maruel to ſee Catholike men ſo vvillingly to loſe land, libertie, credit, life and al for Chriſtes ſake and the Churches faith.

notes.text: Al our good deedes are laid vp vvith God, to be revvarded.

annotations.title: A forme.
annotations.text: The Apoſtles did ſet dovvne a platforme of faith, doctrine, & phraſe of Catholike ſpeach and preaching, & that not ſo much by vvriting (as here vve ſee) as by vvord of mouth: to vvhich he referreth Timothee ouer and aboue his Epiſtles vnto him. ◦ And hovv preciſely Chriſtian Doctors ought to keepe the forme of vvordes aunciently appropriated to the myſteries and matters of our religion, S. Auguſtine expreſſeth in theſe vvordes li. 10 de ciuit. c. 23. Philoſophers ſpeake vvith freedom of vvordes &c. but vve muſt ſpeake according to a certaine rule, leſt licentious libertie of vvordes breede an impious opinion of the things alſo that are ſignified by the ſame. Trinitie, perſon, eſſence, Conſubſtantial, Tranſſubſtantiation, Maſſe, Sacrament, and ſuch like, be verba ſana (as the Apoſtle ſpeaketh) ſound vvordes, giuen to expreſſe certaine high truthes in religion, partly by the Apoſtles and firſt founders of our religion vnder Chriſt, and partly very aptly inuented by holy Councels and fathers, to expreſſe as neere as could be the high ineffable or vnſpeakable veritie of ſome points, and to ſtoppe the Heretikes audacitie and inuention of nevv vvordes and prophane ſpeaches in ſuch things, vvhich the Apoſtle vvarneth Timothee to auoid 1 ep. c. 6, 20. and 2 ep. 2, 16. See the Annotations there.

notes.text: We must speake in Catholike termes, after a certaine rule of faith, and forme of vvordes.

annotations.title: Our Lord.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> To haue this praier of an Apoſtle, or any Prieſt or poore Cath. man ſo relieued, giueth the greateſt hope at the day of our death or general iudgemēt, that can be: and it is vvorth al the landes, honours, and riches of the vvorld.
